title: Finding Your Project — Folders, VS Code, and the Address Bar
description: Where a CodeIgniter project has to sit on disk, how to open it properly in VS Code, and how that folder path turns into a working web address.
congratsText: You can now find, open, and load your project without guessing!
objectives: Locate the single folder WAMP serves and place a project inside it
Build the correct disk path to a CodeIgniter project
Identify what application/, system/, and index.php are each for
Choose the right folder inside application/ for a new file
Open a project in VS Code as a folder, not as a lone file
Apply VS Code shortcuts to move between project files quickly
Translate a folder path into the address that loads it
Diagnose a failed address from what the browser shows
recap: WAMP serves only C:\wamp64\www\ — anything outside it is invisible to the browser.
Each project gets its own folder inside www, and that folder name becomes part of the address.
application/ is your code, system/ is CodeIgniter's engine, index.php is the single entry point.
Controllers, models, views, and config all sit inside application/.
File → Open Folder on the project folder gives you the sidebar; opening one file does not.
Ctrl+Shift+E, Ctrl+P, and Ctrl+` cover most of the moving around you will do.
C:\wamp64\www\ becomes localhost, so a project folder is reached at localhost/foldername.
Apache's Not Found, a bare file listing, and CI3's styled 404 each point at a different mistake.

chunks.text: WAMP serves one folder and one folder only: C:\wamp64\www\. Anything outside it is invisible to the browser.
The order matters. wamp64 comes first, and www sits inside it — not the other way around.
Put your project on the Desktop and the browser cannot reach it, even with the WAMP icon showing green.

chunks.text: Unzip CodeIgniter so its contents land directly in that folder — not inside a second folder with the same name.
Keep the folder name lowercase with no spaces. My Project turns ugly the moment it becomes an address.

sections.title: What You See Inside the Project

chunks.text: Open the project folder and three things matter: application/, system/, and index.php.
application/ is yours. Everything you write this term goes somewhere inside it.
system/ is CodeIgniter's engine. You may read it; you do not edit it.

quiz.question: Type the name of the folder that holds your own controllers, models, and views.

sections.title: The Folders You Will Open All Term

chunks.text: Inside application/ you will live in four folders: controllers/, models/, views/, and config/.
A controller file starts with a capital letter — Pivot.php, never pivot.php.
routes.php and database.php both live in the config folder.

quiz.question: You are told to create the PHP class that will handle a new page. Which folder do you create it in?

sections.title: Opening It Properly in VS Code

chunks.text: Use File → Open Folder and pick your project. Opening a single file gives you no sidebar to move around in.

check.question: Which one gives you the file tree?

chunks.text: Pick the project folder itself, not www — otherwise you scroll past every other project on the machine.
Faster route: right-click the project folder in File Explorer and choose Open with Code.

quiz.question: Arrange the steps to open your project in VS Code the right way.
tokens: check application/ appears in the sidebar
correctOrder: check application/ appears in the sidebar

chunks.text: The Explorer sidebar (Ctrl+Shift+E) is your folder tree. Expand application/ once and leave it expanded.
Ctrl+P, then a few letters of a filename, jumps straight there — no folder clicking at all.
Ctrl+` opens a terminal that already starts inside your project folder.

quiz.question: Type the VS Code shortcut that jumps straight to a file by typing part of its name.

sections.title: From Folder Path to Web Address

chunks.text: The browser never types out C:\wamp64\www\. That whole part becomes one word: localhost.
So the folder C:\wamp64\www\karinderya is loaded at localhost/karinderya.
The slashes flip, too. Disk paths lean one way, addresses lean the other.

quiz.question: Your project sits at C:\wamp64\www\clinic. What do you type in the address bar to load it?

chunks.text: Apache's plain Not Found page means the folder name you typed does not match a folder inside www.

check.question: Apache's Not Found points at:
options: a typo in the folder name

chunks.text: A bare list of file names means WAMP found the folder but no index.php inside it.

check.question: A file listing on screen means:

chunks.text: CI3's own styled 404 page is different news entirely: WAMP and CodeIgniter both ran, and only the controller is missing.

quiz.question: You typed an address and got a bare list of file names. Arrange the checks in the order you should do them.
tokens: open that folder in File Explorer
confirm the folder name in the address
point the address one folder deeper
correctOrder: confirm the folder name in the address

chunks.text: The same project shows up three ways: a path in File Explorer, a folder open in VS Code, and an address in the browser.
Rename the folder and all three shift at once — the old address stops working immediately.
Keep all three open side by side. Most "it doesn't work" moments are simply one of them pointing elsewhere.

quiz.question: You rename your project folder from clinic to barangay_clinic. What has to be updated as a result?
options: Only the address bar; VS Code re-points by itself
The address bar, and the folder open in VS Code
The system/ folder and the application/ folder
Nothing — WAMP keeps serving the old name
